content: Write a performance review for a sales rep who exceeded quota but struggled with paperwork.

# Annual Performance Review

**Employee:** [Name]
**Title:** Account Executive, Mid-Market
**Reviewer:** [Manager Name]
**Review Period:** January 1 – December 31, [Year]
**Date:** [Date]

**Overall Rating:** Exceeds Expectations (with development area noted)

---

## Summary

[Name] delivered an outstanding year of revenue performance, finishing at **127% of annual quota ($2.54M against a $2.0M target)** and ranking second on a team of nine. He consistently wins competitive deals, builds genuine trust with buyers, and is the person teammates seek out when a negotiation stalls.

That commercial strength is offset by persistent gaps in administrative execution — CRM hygiene, deal documentation, expense reporting, and forecast submissions. These are not cosmetic issues: they have created downstream problems for forecasting accuracy, deal desk turnaround, and his own commission processing. Closing this gap is the single highest-leverage change [Name] can make in the coming year, both for the team and for his own advancement.

---

## Key Accomplishments

- **Quota attainment:** 127% of plan; four of four quarters at or above target.
- **New logo acquisition:** Closed 14 new accounts, including [Account A] ($310K ACV), the largest new-business win in the region this year.
- **Win rate:** 34% on qualified opportunities, against a team average of 26%.
- **Expansion:** Grew [Account B] from $45K to $128K through a well-executed multi-threading strategy that he later shared in a team enablement session.
- **Customer feedback:** Named specifically in three customer reference calls as a reason the buyer chose us. Post-sale CSAT on his accounts averaged 4.7/5.
- **Team contribution:** Volunteered to mentor two new hires during ramp; both attained quota in their first full quarter.

**Strengths observed:** Discovery and qualification, executive presence, competitive positioning, resilience after losses, willingness to help peers.

---

## Development Area: Administrative Execution and CRM Discipline

Specific observations from the review period:

- **Forecast submissions:** Late in 9 of 12 months, typically by 2–4 days. On three occasions, missing data required [Manager] to reconstruct pipeline figures manually before the regional roll-up.
- **CRM data quality:** Opportunity close dates and next steps were stale in approximately 40% of open deals at any given time (team average: 12%). Two deals closed in the quarter without contract values updated, which distorted Q3 forecast accuracy by roughly $180K.
- **Deal documentation:** Incomplete handoff notes on five closed-won accounts required Customer Success to re-interview the customer on scope and commitments. One instance created a misalignment on implementation timeline that took three weeks to resolve.
- **Expense and commission paperwork:** Q2 commission payment was delayed by one pay cycle due to unsubmitted deal approval forms. Expense reports were submitted an average of 41 days after incurrence, against a 30-day policy.

**Why this matters:** Revenue results are excellent, but the surrounding process is how the business plans headcount, recognizes revenue, and serves customers after the sale. Right now, [Name]'s administrative gaps are being absorbed by his manager, deal desk, and CS partners. That is not sustainable, and it is currently the primary barrier to consideration for a Senior AE or team lead role, both of which carry responsibility for modeling process discipline for others.

---

## Goals for [Next Year]

| # | Goal | Measure | Target Date |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Achieve 100%+ quota attainment | Revenue against plan | Ongoing |
| 2 | On-time forecast submission | 11 of 12 months submitted by deadline | Monthly |
| 3 | CRM hygiene | ≥90% of open opportunities with current close date, next step, and stage at each Friday audit | Weekly |
| 4 | Complete handoff documentation | 100% of closed-won deals with completed handoff template before kickoff call | Per deal |
| 5 | Expense compliance | All reports submitted within 30 days | Monthly |

---

## Agreed Action Plan

1. **Time blocking:** [Name] will block 30 minutes at 4:30 p.m. each Friday for CRM updates and pipeline review, treated as a non-negotiable calendar commitment.
2. **Manager check-in:** Weekly 1:1s will open with a five-minute pipeline hygiene review for the first 90 days, then move to biweekly if metrics hold.
3. **Tooling support:** [Name] will complete the mobile CRM logging training in January and enable automated activity capture, which should reduce manual entry substantially.
4. **Administrative support:** Requesting approval for [Name] to use [X hours/month] of sales support resource for proposal formatting and document assembly — a reasonable investment given his revenue leverage. Note: this supports the workflow but does not transfer ownership of forecast accuracy or CRM data.
5. **90-day review point:** Progress on Goals 2–5 will be formally reviewed on [Date]. Sustained improvement over two consecutive quarters is the stated prerequisite for Senior AE consideration.

---

## Manager Comments

[Name] is a genuinely talented seller and one of the reasons this region hit plan. I want to be direct: the selling is not the question this year, and I do not want the administrative feedback to obscure how strong the results are. The question is whether he can pair that talent with the operational reliability the next role requires. I believe he can — the issues are habit and prioritization, not capability or attitude, and he has responded to this feedback constructively when we've discussed it informally. The action plan above is designed to make the habit easier to build rather than to add oversight for its own sake.

---

## Employee Comments

_[Space for employee response]_

---

**Employee Signature:** ______________________ **Date:** __________

**Manager Signature:** ______________________ **Date:** __________

---

*Note: Swap in your actual metrics, dates, and examples — specific, documented instances make the development feedback defensible and far more useful to the employee than general characterizations. If your organization ties ratings to compensation bands, confirm that "Exceeds Expectations" is consistent with the merit or commission outcome you intend before delivering this.*
I want to see this written for a different reader than the first version. Rewrite it for a reader who already knows the background.

**Assumption:** I've written this for your second-line reviewer — the VP who already knows [Name], the territory, the number, and the paperwork history, and who is reading this to make a calibration and promotion decision. So: no recap, no explaining why CRM hygiene matters, and it leads with the ask. If you meant the employee as the informed reader, see the note at the end.

---

**MEMO**

**To:** [VP, Sales]
**From:** [Manager]
**Re:** [Name] — year-end rating and the Senior AE question
**Date:** [Date]

**Recommendation:** Exceeds Expectations. Not recommending Senior AE this cycle. Recommending an explicit 90-day gate with a decision point at [Date].

**The number.** 127%, $2.54M on $2.0M, four of four quarters, #2 of nine. [Account A] at $310K ACV. 34% win rate against 26% team average. Both of his ramp mentees hit plan in their first full quarter. No argument here.

**What's changed since we discussed this mid-year.** Nothing material. Forecast late in 9 of 12 months. CRM staleness holding around 40% of open deals against a 12% team average. The ~$180K Q3 forecast variance was his data, not market movement. Five incomplete CS handoffs, one of which cost three weeks on the [Account C] implementation timeline. Q2 commission delayed a full cycle on his own unsubmitted approval forms.

**Why not Senior AE.** The role owns process modeling for the ramp cohort. He is currently a net consumer of deal desk capacity and my time rather than a contributor to standards. Promoting him now also sends the wrong signal to the two reps he mentored, both of whom carry clean pipelines.

**Why not a lower rating.** The revenue is real and the gap is habit and prioritization, not capability or attitude. A Meets is defensible on paper and probably costs us the rep — he has options and knows it. I'd rather hold the rating and make the gate unambiguous.

**What I need from you.**

- Sign-off on Exceeds with the development note attached as written.
- Approval for [X hrs/month] of sales support for proposal and document assembly. Cheap against his revenue leverage. Forecast accuracy and CRM ownership stay with him — the support is workflow, not transfer.
- Confirmation that Exceeds lands where I think it does in the merit band. I don't want the comp outcome contradicting the message.
- Your read on stating the 90-day gate to him in those words. My instinct is yes, plainly.

**The gate.** On-time forecast 11 of 12 months. ≥90% CRM hygiene at the Friday audit. 100% handoff template completion pre-kickoff. Expenses inside 30 days. Two consecutive clean quarters before Senior AE goes back on the table.

**Delivery.** 1:1 on [Date]. Number first, then the gate, no sandwiching. I expect he takes it constructively; he has each time so far.

---

*If the informed reader you had in mind was [Name] himself, the same compression applies but the emphasis shifts: cut the accomplishments list to a sentence, cut the rationale-for-rating entirely, and spend the space on the four gate metrics and what specifically comes off his plate via sales support. Tell me which and I'll rework it.*
I need a shorter version of this for a different placement. Cut it to about half the length and lead with the main point.

**Assumption:** Same reader (VP), tighter slot — a calibration packet entry or an email she reads on her phone. Same content, roughly half the words.

---

**Re: [Name] — Exceeds Expectations, no Senior AE this cycle. Recommending a 90-day gate with a decision point [Date].**

**Number:** 127%, $2.54M on $2.0M, four of four quarters, #2 of nine. 34% win rate vs. 26% team. [Account A] at $310K. Both ramp mentees hit plan.

**Gap:** Unchanged since mid-year. Forecast late 9 of 12 months. CRM staleness ~40% of open deals vs. 12% team average. The ~$180K Q3 variance was his data, not the market. Five incomplete CS handoffs, one costing three weeks on [Account C]. Q2 commission delayed a cycle on his own unsubmitted forms.

**Rationale:** Senior AE owns process modeling for the ramp cohort; he's currently a net consumer of deal desk and my time. But the revenue is real and the gap is habit, not capability — a Meets is defensible on paper and probably costs us the rep. Hold the rating, make the gate unambiguous.

**Gate:** On-time forecast 11 of 12. ≥90% CRM hygiene at Friday audit. 100% handoff templates pre-kickoff. Expenses inside 30 days. Two clean quarters before Senior AE returns to the table.

**Need from you:** (1) Sign-off on Exceeds with the development note attached. (2) [X hrs/month] sales support for document assembly — workflow only, CRM and forecast ownership stay with him. (3) Confirm Exceeds lands where I think it does in the merit band. (4) Your read on stating the gate to him in these words; my instinct is yes, plainly.
We can't include a claim about results in this one, for reasons on our end. Take out the claim about results and leave everything else as it is.

**One flag before the text:** removing the results claim leaves the rating and the rationale resting on an unstated premise. "Exceeds Expectations" and "the gap is habit, not capability" both implicitly assert strong performance, and a calibration reader will ask what the rating is based on. I've left them in as instructed, but if the constraint is that the figures can't be stated *anywhere*, the recommendation may not stand on its own — you'd likely need to point to the number in a separate system of record and reference it, or defer the rating. Your call; you know the reason on your end.

I also left the ~$180K Q3 variance in, since it's evidence of the documentation gap rather than a performance result. Say the word if that needs to go too.
